chapters.html:
If being adored was a drug, Phainon had no regrets getting high off it.

It gave him purpose. It made him feel the most like himself because he could be anything in anyone's mind. He played a hundred different roles in a hundred different minds; for admiration is constructing an image of someone from nothing but their shadow. There was no need to know the person behind the sunny smile and sky blue eyes since his admirers knew him as whoever they wanted him to be.

The distance was perfect, so why did he feel like a little kid sitting alone on the swings— watching everyone else laugh and play without him?

No. not this again, get a grip. You are not some poor soul forced into a life of suffering through this role. You chose it. You will bear it— just like how you shall bear the hopes of the organisation.

Perhaps the only two people close enough to him to be considered friends were Castorice and Hyacine—both of whose seats were empty when he entered the mostly vacant meeting room. He supposed Castorice had overslept again after staying up all night writing or drawing. Hyacine was probably called to the med bay— too nice to refuse treating yet another patient. Or she was helping out as Prof A's teaching assistant. It was also on him for arriving far too early.

Phainon was a recruit at the CHRYSOS organisation, an institute dedicated to training exceptional individuals to fight against Black Tide creatures. The program involved everything from sending the recruits on missions for experience to in class lectures and physical training.

Okhema was the last civilisation that remained. Nobody was allowed outside and the only outsiders allowed were refugees. Outside the safe haven of Okhema, the Black Tide monsters lurked, ending civilisations. One of them was his hometown of Aedes Elysiae.

Frankly, it was too small to be considered a town— but as a child, it was his whole world.

He was picked up by Aglaea when he was about seventeen— or maybe sixteen. He doesn't remember when. His memories from that particular period of his life were sparse and littered with things he'd rather not look back on.

This was his final year in the training program before he graduated and went out into the world as a real agent. And he would pass with flying colours— Phainon would make sure of it.

Earlier, Professor Anaxa had informed the class that there would be a new recruit joining them. For someone to join the program this late, they would have to be incredibly talented or incredibly stupid. Phainon bet on the latter, for no one in their right mind would possibly think they could keep up with the rest of the class— all of whom had been training for years.

There sat another person in the meeting room, a few rows of chairs in front of Phainon. The stranger had blonde hair dyed red at the ends. It reminded Phainon of fire, captivating but too intimidating to approach. From behind, it looked as though he was wearing a black leather jacket and had a bit of his hair in a braid that fell onto his right shoulder. Phainon didn't remember seeing such a unique silhouette around the facility before, so he knew this must be the new recruit Prof A. mentioned.

Phainon brushed off invisible specks of dust from his shirt and straightened his outfit. His entire wardrobe was curated by Aglaea to shield innocent bystander's eyes from his atrocious fashion sense— he didn't think his sense of fashion was that bad, but he acquiesced in her command anyways. With a confident stride, he headed to the row the new guy was seated at.

He didn't think he'd ever seen someone look so striking before. His hair from up close looked like a lion's mane and his eyes were a striking gold. Everything about the man seemed.. gilded.

It certainly didn't help that he was intimidatingly attractive.

Phainon walked over to the pretty strawberry blonde haired guy and gave him a light, easy smile. Most people would smile back, but this stranger gave no acknowledgement of his presence. Tough audience, but Phainon had full confidence in winning this person over.

"So, are you new here?"

"Yes."

Well, this guy was rather curt. No matter, this did not faze him in the slightest.

"Well, pleasure to meet you! My name's Phainon"

"I don't have time for pleasantries. I'm here to graduate from this training program and top the rankings."

How presumptuous.

"I'm afraid you have your work cut out for you"

"Why so?"

"Because the undisputed top ranker is standing right in front of you." Phainon said in the most amiable voice he could muster without it sounding like he was planning murder. The new guy was getting on his nerves. The blonde scoffed and stood up, his eyes level with Phainon's.

Damn, the guy was tall and built as hell—

Phainon's brain cut him off from that train of thought as quickly as it could.

"What, so you think I can't beat you?"

"I think you'll find that incredibly difficult, Not saying that you can't, but for now, keep dreaming big."

"Is that a challenge?"

Something wild flashed in the blonde's eyes, daring Phainon to fight back.

Phainon returned the glare with a brilliant smile and poison coated by a sugary voice as he replied,"Would you like it to be?"

"Don't beg me to reconsider once I've begun the fight."

"As if I would. Unless, of course, you back down because you're too scared."

The stranger's fist was the first to fly, going straight for Phainon's jaw. Phainon dodged it and tried to land a kick on the other guy's side. The effortless way in which the stranger blocked the kick and struck a blow on Phainon's shoulder sent Phainon's mind reeling and he was pretty sure it wasn't because of the punch.

This guy could actually keep up with Phainon. Worst of all, it felt like he had an equal chance of winning. He was strong— stronger than anybody Phainon had ever come across. Blows were traded— some landed and some deflected. Phainon's ribcage throbbed, but he didn't care.

That was the most alive Phainon had felt in years.

In their scuffle, they had tumbled to the front of the meeting room, which was where Professor Anaxa found them.

"No fighting in the meeting room." A stern voice cut through the air, making Phainon and the blonde stranger pause. The stranger reluctantly let go of the collar of Phainon's shirt and Phainon

Well, there went Phainon's dignity.

It sure was nice while it lasted.

"I'm sorry, Professor Anaxa" Phainon gritted out, cringing at his feeble attempt to salvage his pride. At least nobody else in the facility was present to see the fight.

Anaxa sighed heavily and Phainon realised he hit a nerve with that apology. It was probably because he called him Professor Anaxa instead of Professor Anaxagoras. Anaxa— no— Anaxagoras was surprisingly touchy when it came to his name.

"Phainon, Mydeimos— you two are adults. This is not a place where you can brawl like children. Do you understand?"

"Yes, I understand. Although, I'd prefer you call me Mydei." The annoying guy— what's his name? Mydeimos? —answered.

Mydeimos… now where had he heard that name before?

Wait.

As if on cue, Phainon's brain supplied year old memories of him watching the news where they reported the death of Castrum Kremnos' dictator. Killed by his son Mydeimos— the reporter had said— it seems the bloodline's legacy of patricide continues. Mydeimos had chosen to abdicate the role of the next dictator and left the citizens of Kremnos under the protection of Okhema's government.

The very same Mydeimos was glaring daggers into Phainon's skull, like he was itching to get one last punch in.

Phainon, you fool— of course he'd be capable of joining the training program this late. He's just that powerful and experienced. He led an army, you nitwit.

Phainon wondered if he had enough time to make a run for it and jump into oncoming traffic.

Anaxa cleared his throat and looked expectantly at Phainon, like he was supposed to say something. Phainon took a second to pray to every Titan out there to save him from this situation before mumbling his apologies.

"I too understand. This will not happen again."

Anaxa did not look mollified by his apologies. "Phainon, I expect you to share the coursework covered so far in this term and accompany Mydei in getting settled."

This day could not get any worse. Mydeimos looked just as horrified, an even deeper scowl etching itself into his features. It would do him some good to smile more— maybe then the guy would look a lot more approachable and a lot less like he was saying 'I want to kill you where you stand and quite possibly harvest your organs'.

Professor Anaxa sent them back to their seats as the rest of the recruits started to file in. Phainon trudged back to his seat and flopped onto the chair. Bad move, because he was pretty sure he bruised his tailbone on the hard metal. Darn the facility for its uncomfortable furniture. But as the greetings began, he plastered on his default charm.

"Morning, Phainon!"

"Good morning, Danae!"

"How's it going, Phainon?"

"It's going great, Cyrones!"

There. This was easy. This was familiar.

A soft voice sounded from behind him.

"Hey, Phainon."

"Ah, Cas! So you didn't oversleep after all"

Castorice cracked a small smile "Apparently not"

"Say, who's that new student over there?" Hyacine asked, placing her bag decorated with a multitude of charms and pins on the floor and taking her seat. A pair of bows tied her hair up into its signature ponytails.

"That's Mydeimos." Phainon said, trying his best to hide his contempt for the guy.

"No way— you mean that Mydeimos?"

"Yes, that Mydeimos."

"Interesting. I heard he's quite skilled in hand to hand combat. His fighting style must be like yours then" Castorice mused

Phainon internally grimaced. Indeed, Mydeimos' fighting style was like his — but he seemed to focus more on strength than speed, unlike Phainon. That meant his punches and kicks hurt, as evidenced by the throbbing pain on his body.

Phainon gave a weak laugh "I'm supposed to 'show him around' and share the course material with him"

Castorice's mouth formed an 'o' shape and Hyacine nodded solemnly

"Yeah, good luck with that."

I'll need the luck, Phainon thought to himself after the lecture was over. The walk to Mydeimos' seat felt like a walk to the gallows. He could see it in his mind's eye— a man marching over to the guillotine that he was inevitably sentenced to.

"Hey, Mydeimos?"

"I prefer to be called Mydei."

"Right, right. Uh… I'll need your number"

Mydei raised an eyebrow, looked up from his phone and deadpanned "Don't you think it's a bit too early for that?"

Phainon blushed, his smile faltering.

"I didn't mean that. I need some sort of contact information so I can reach you."

"I'll give you my email address."

"Cool!"

Phainon hoped his grin didn't look as painful as it felt.

Mydei scoffed, but wrote down his email address on a sheet of paper. His handwriting was just as neat and as put together as he was.

Phainon was irrationally jealous of how self assured Mydei seemed. Mydei didn't look like he had ever felt anxious of what other people thought of him and wonder if he was even worthy of their praise. He clearly never practised smiling in the mirror until his cheeks hurt and he had perfected a winning smile. He never had to wear the perfect smile and say the perfect things and wonder if the real him even existed anymore.

Lucky bastard.

Professor Anaxa was waiting for Phainon outside the door. He corrected the eye patch over his eye before affixing Phainon with a stern glare with his good eye.

"Phainon, you should know that I do not take kindly to violence within the facility. This may not be a proper educational institute, but fighting a fellow recruit is unacceptable. You are incredibly lucky that you're getting only a warning and that nobody else was there to report this incident. I let Mydei off since he's new, but you should really know better."

Phainon flinched slightly, regretting how defensive he got. "I'm sorry— wait, why is Mydei getting let off? Isn't equality what you stand for? Why isn't he getting reprimanded too?"

"Mydei has his reasons for joining this late and I highly doubt that he's familiar with Okhema's customs."

"But how—"

"Phainon. I recall giving you multiple pardons when you first joined the facility. Is it not equality if Mydei gets the same treatment?"

Phainon sucked in a breath, wincing as he remembered his past self's stand-offishness and difficulty in adjusting.

Great. Now Phainon's embarrassed himself in front of Professor Anaxa for the second time in under an hour.

Anaxa sighed "I hope you understand now. Since you came here from Aedes Elysiae, you know what it's like to be new. I expect you to try to get along with Mydei, even if guiding him around is too difficult a task for you." He turned around after he took a few steps away "Don't forget to share the lecture notes with Mydei. I can count on you to do that, yes?"

"Yes" Phainon replied.

The sting of embarrassment would not leave him even as the day progressed. It felt like he was swallowing something bitter over and over again. His stomach curdled every time he recollected the time he lost his composure.

On the topic of doing things he regretted, Phainon also regretted claiming to be the top ranker in the facility. Sure, he was the best at fighting and excelled in debates, but there truly wasn't much else to him. For all he cared, he was top ranker only in name and popularity.

He did consider, at some point, sending a message to Castorice and Hyacine about his current predicament, but didn't follow through with it. Castorice was busy in the labs and Hyacine was working in the med bay or assisting Professor Anaxa and Phainon wasn't sure if they'd want to hear him be pathetic.

Flopping onto his bed after a day made excruciating, Phainon wanted nothing more than to collapse and go to sleep.

However, he still had to send a certain blonde haired man the lecture notes of the past few weeks. He drafted a message and hit send.

Here are the notes for the lectures. No need to thank me.

Attachment

"And that's why I have a bruise on my left shoulder." Phainon recounted to a very unimpressed Hyacine who had to treat his wounds after a full day of them getting too painful to ignore.

"You should've come for treatment yesterday, Phainon" Hyacine reprimanded like a disappointed parent. Phainon tried to not look too upset about being scolded— even if he hated it when people were disappointed in him.

"I know"

"Although I must say, I have never seen you despise someone as much as you do Mydei, let alone hate anyone at all."

"Look at him, Hyacine. He's the problem."

"So you're intimidated by him? Threatened by his presence? Is it like some wild animal adjacent thing in which you get possessive over your territory and position—"

"—NO! No— he gets on my nerves is all."

"Uh huh." Hyacine hummed, regarding Phainon with a bemused glance. Phainon couldn't believe he was being compared to a wild animal. Sure, humans were just evolved wild animals with a consciousness, but that didn't stop him from feeling insulted.

Hyacine packed up the gauze and ointment "All done! You can go now. For the love of Kephale, don't ignore your wounds next time." She shuffled over to the counter and began organising the tools there and continued "You should have told me about the whole Mydei situation sooner."

Phainon smiled and gingerly prodded his dressed wounds.

"Sure, I'll do that next time."

He could tell Hyacine didn't believe his words. He didn't either.

He definitely regretted having to limp around the rest of the day, brushing off others' concerns for his health. He was fine, just a bit banged up. Mydei was nowhere to be seen. A petty part of Phainon hoped he was just as wounded as he was.

That evening, he got a call from Castorice.

"Phainon?"

"Yeah, hi! What's up?"

"I heard from Cinny you got into a fight with Mydei."

"Yeah."

"When were you going to tell us? Had you not chosen to get treatment, would we have never found out?" She asked, reproachful

"I swear, I would've told you—"

"—You wouldn't have—"

"Sorry."

Castorice sighed heavily. Great. Now he's disappointed three people and it was all because of Mydei's arrival.

"Look, we care. We want to be there if you need help. If that includes help at beating him in the next ranked mission, so be it"

"Seriously?"

"Yes."

Phainon wanted to believe her, he truly did. But would Castorice still choose to help Phainon if she knew what he'd done and who he'd been?

Would she still spend long nights talking to him and Hyacine about her latest creation? Would she still see him as a friend she could tell anything and everything to?

Phainon really, really didn't want to know the answer to that question, so he laughed lightly and said, "Thanks, I'll keep that in mind."

Castorice stayed true to her word, handing Phainon a few vials of poisons that she said would immobilise the Black Tide creatures.

She was lucky— she didn't have to undergo training meant for fighting in the front lines. She preferred experimenting with poisons and working in the lab. Professor Anaxa had discovered Castorice's natural talent a few years ago and immediately sent in an appeal to have her work in the labs.

Castorice loved working in the labs. For as long as Phainon had known her, she'd always been withdrawn— so her expressing a love for something was incredibly rare. He was glad she found something that resonated with her.

There was this shine that some people seemed to have when they were truly passionate about something. When they find that piece of themself, it would carve itself into their soul, wire their brains permanently. It would live longer then they, outlasting death— forever immortalised under their name.

That wholeness was something Phainon would never get to feel, but he felt close to it when he won.

So he'd have to get the highest ranking in the mission because winning would restore his dignity.

Maybe he'd jinxed it because there was no way this was happening.

Phainon was to be paired with Mydei. His phone screen seemed to mock him as he read the assignment partner list sent by Tribios over and over again. The poisons Castorice had provided him with felt redundant.

There was no way in Amphoreus' twelve titans that this was real. He tried to convince himself that it was all an oddly realistic fever dream. Or better yet, have hidden cameras pop out of the walls and have someone yell 'gotcha!' because this was some elaborate prank.

Unfortunately, Phainon was not high off his rocker or being played a fool.

Mydei walked into the briefing room at that exact time, his eyes burning holes into his phone. Overall, Mydei looked just as displeased to be paired up with him as Phainon was. Displeased may have been under exaggerating the murderous looks being thrown his way. Phainon would like to hold onto his organs, thank you very much.

"I'm not any happier about this than you are." Phainon sniffed.

"Evidently." Mydei retorted before sitting on the chair next to Phainon.

The room fell silent as Tribios, a mentor at CHRYSOS, entered. She would be the one conducting the briefing for the mission.

Phainon shot up and stumbled slightly as he made his way over to her "Miss Tribios— is there any chance we can change our partners for this mission?"

"Why? Is there a problem with being partnered up with Mydei?"

Yes, Phainon's brain screamed, there is a very big, Mydei- sized problem.

But the others in the room were looking at him curiously and he knew that one wrong word could send his reputation straight to the gallows. So he sucked it up and shook his head, feigning innocence "No, no not all. I'm sorry for disturbing you."

He fled back to his seat in the most dignified manner possible, considering the eyes trained on him.

"No luck in getting rid of me, huh?" Mydei asked, looking at Phainon through the corner of his eye.

Phainon was too peeved to respond.

Mydei— 1 , Phainon— 0

Mydei sat in silence through the rest of the briefing and remained stone faced as they geared up for their mission in the locker room. Phainon tried to focus on pulling his shirt over his head, but his gaze was drawn to Mydei as he pulled off his turtleneck.

Oh titans, his body was ridiculous.

Red tattoos that resembled fire curled around his body. His muscles looked even better than they did with his shirt on—

Nope— not going there— Phainon's brain interrupted his train of thought and he wrenched his eyes away from Mydei. He busied himself with packing his bag and weapons. It was always a struggle to put on his gear— but any distraction was a welcome one.

If Phainon noticed Mydei's eyes scrutinising his own body, he made no remark.

For once, Phainon decided to forgo small talk and keep his mouth shut as they walked out the doors of the CHRYSOS facility. The sun beat down on them relentlessly and the city hummed with life beyond them. Skyscrapers lined the view, cars zooming past. Each time he saw the city, it felt like the first time he had set foot in Okhema.

As Phainon fumbled around his pocket for his identity card to board the subway, Mydei held up a hand.

"My bike." Mydei said, although it sounded more like a demand than an offer.

Talk about picking your poison.

He was essentially trading being gawked at with being in close proximity with Mydei. To be fair, public transport would too crowded with all the people swarming to talk to him and take pictures— such was the price of fame.

Phainon rarely ever went to the garage provided by the facility, given that he didn't have a vehicle to call his own. Mydei's bike was a sleek black motorbike whose brand a plebeian such as Phainon could not recognise. Mydei tossed a helmet at Phainon, not caring if he got socked in the face.

That was probably reason number nine hundred and ninety nine for why Phainon hated Mydei.

Phainon cursed under his breath, dreading the ride. He should have just taken public transport.

It wasn't long before they were zipping through the streets of Okhema at breakneck speeds.

"If you wanted to break my ribcage, you have a hundred more efficient means to do so. I don't see why you're so fixated on this one" Mydei said dryly

"Shut. Up." Phainon gritted out, not caring that his grip around Mydei's waist was suffocating. The wind howled against his ears as they broke the speed limit, multiple laws and basic road safety rules.

"You're just afraid."

"Of dying? Well, I'm sorry I want to live!" Phainon yelled, flinching every time they went over a speed breaker. Nothing seemed to faze Mydei, not even the very real threat of death, apparently.

Mydei scoffed derisively.

The bike screeched as Mydei pulled up to the walls that enclosed Okhema city. The two hour subway transit was shortened to a mere thirty minutes. Thirty minutes of suffering on Phainon's end, but thirty minutes all the same. Phainon stumbled off the bike and never had he loved the ground as much as he did in that moment.

Phainon took out a hilt that expanded and transformed into his pride and joy — the sword Dawnmaker. Mydei just stood there, unimpressed.

"You gonna go in and fight with your bare fists?" Phainon asked, bemused. Most recruits used weapons of some sort, so someone going in with nothing but their bare fists sounded like a death sentence to Phainon. However, Mydei himself was the walking definition of a death sentence.

Mydei frowned "Yes."

"Good luck with that"

Mydei turned on his heel, only to vault over the wall. Phainon gaped— that was been a twenty foot wall at the very least, and Mydei effortlessly scaled it.

Show off. Especially when there was a perfectly functional gate to use. Phainon chose to use the gate like a woefully normal person to find Mydei already locked in battle with Black Tide creatures.

Turned out, he did fight with his fists after all. And Phainon would be damned if he said the way Mydei fought wasn't impressive. Mydei moved with a ferocity and grace that was unparalleled. Seeing him fight— actually fight and not wrestle— was a surreal experience. Mydei was essentially a blur of gold and red, with his battle armor glinting under the sun. He was the very embodiment of fire— unpredictable and mesmerising.

But Phainon wasn't going to fall behind so easily. He still had Castorice's poisons on hand and this might be his chance to win against Mydei, even if it was a small win. He lunged at the first prowling Black Tide creature he laid his eyes on and sliced through it cleanly. Its eyes flashed with an undecipherable emotion before it crumpled to the ground.

Wait.

Eyes?

Black Tide creatures weren't supposed to have eyes. They were the Black Tide clothed in armor. Phainon was hallucinating this. He had to be. The ride must have messed up his sense of cognition or something.

That night, Phainon dreamed of a past long gone.

Phainon sat on a branch of the oak tree in the fields of Aedes Elysiae. The wind chimes strung on the tree by him and his friends clinked along to the breeze. The sky was a molten yellow, streaked with hues of fiery red. The sun steadily sank below the horizon, going to sleep for yet another night.

"Phainon! Come on, Ma's calling us for dinner!" A sweet voice called him.

The pink haired girl, Cyrene, waved at Phainon, beckoning him over. Phainon started climbing down the huge tree and stalked through the wheat fields. The season to harvest the wheat was drawing near, which meant sometimes helping his parents under the stars. After he approached Cyrene, she gave him a once over and dusted leaves out of his overalls and hair.

Cyrene plucked one last leaf from his hair and announced,"There, you're presentable now." Phainon giggled as she pinched his cheeks and took his sister's hand as she led him inside.

His parents' muffled voices could be heard from the kitchen

"The black tide's breaching civilisations. The village head's contacted the Holy City. They told us to lay low and stay in Aedes Elysiae. They said it wasn't a threat and we would be safe. Are we, though?"

"I heard about a Black Tide monster in the forests nearby. Should we consider leaving? "

"And leave our livelihood and where our children will grow up? We won't have any money to settle and I doubt any city would be willing to take us in."

"But—"

"Mom!" Cyrene called.

"Cyrene! Did you get Phainon to come inside?" His mother said.

"Yes, Ma! I'm back! Hi Pa!" Phainon exclaimed, hopping around on one foot as he tugged his boot off his right foot.

"Hello to you too." His father walked over to him and ruffled his hair. Laughing heartily, he headed over to the dining table."Come on, get over here."

"He's gonna get to the table once he gets his shoes off" Cyrene said, jogging away from him as he struggled to get his boots off.

"Hey! Don't leave me!"

His cozy little home faded into a pinprick of light as Cyrene kept running from him. Phainon stumbled after her, trying to catch up. But she kept moving farther away from him and no matter how hard he tried, he couldn't catch her. Tears streamed down his cheeks as he sobbed, his footsteps growing sluggish before he crumpled to the ground. It felt like he was sinking in quicksand, his limbs no different from metal.

Black crystals consumed what little light the place had as the unmistakable stench of blood permeated his nostrils. Phainon tried to close his eyes, only to have them forced open to face a different scene.

The streets of Styxia— the abandoned metropolis — was the first thing he saw as his eyes adjusted to the light of the broken neon signs littered around. The smell of smog mixed in with the stench of blood. Loud sirens blared in the distance. There was nary a soul in sight, all of the other refugees or scavengers who had chanced upon the ruins.

Nobody questioned why there was a thirteen year old with dusty white hair and skin that clung too tight to his bones walking among them. They didn't look him in the eye or approach him, for kindness was a resource not many could spare. He spent those years killing Black Tide monsters and scavenging for survival, when he should've lived out his teenage years as a normal person.

He looked down at his bloodied hands, stained with the corrosion of the Black Tide as he stood over a pile of corpses. It wasn't an uncommon sight to see a desecrated corpse lying on the ground. Phainon tried not to think that that corpse once had dreams, wishes and a life. They were once someone's family, friend, lover. It felt so strange to have one's life there one minute and then taken the next, like all they had experienced in their life was irrelevant.

He slumped against a wall, holding back more tears from falling.

One of the corpses looked up at him— a pair of bloodshot eyes making contact with his as the world crumbled all over again.

He now knew where he'd seen those bloodshot eyes before. The Black Tide creature in that mission with Mydei had the very same eyes. That thing looked too human for him to ignore.

He felt sick to his stomach.

Without thinking, he called Aglaea. His hands were shaking as she picked up.

"Hello?" Her voice sounded from the other line.

"That monster— all the Black Tide monsters— what are they? Why did one of them have eyes?"

"Phainon, we have never heard of a Black Tide creature that could have eyes."

"Then what did I see? Aglaea— what did I witness?"

"… I think this is a case of a mutated Black Tide monster. I've seen a few of them before. You've learned about them in the training program, I believe. Mutations usually come in the form of extra limbs and powers. Although, eyes must be another unique variety."

Phainon felt stupid, like he was a child seeking reassurance. "Really?"

"Yes. Really. I'll look into it further, though."

"Oh."

"…Do you need a break? Take rest over the weekend and I'll arrange a break from Monday. "

"No. I— I'm fine. I just had a dream. It's nothing, really. I'm sorry for bothering you."

"Phainon—"

He cut the call, unable to bear the shame that welled up in his gut. He'd let the pressure get to him and he'd lost it. He usually kept these paranoid breaks in character to himself, forcing himself to relive those moments until he either no longer felt them anymore or they consumed him entirely.

His throat constricted, and he felt himself physically recoil as the embarrassment hit him waves. He'd gotten ahead of himself and let his paranoia win. Maybe it was because it was his first time actually seeing one of these mutations.

He was losing his grip.

Phainon got out of bed with great difficulty and got himself ready before heading out of the room to get himself something to eat. It was already midday and he'd slept through the morning.

Mydei was already at the stove, making some fancy vegetable dish Phainon couldn't recognise.

Phainon veered around and tried to retreat, but Mydei's voice cut through the air.

"Sit. Lunch is almost ready."

Huh? Mydei— making lunch for him? Was this a part of his dream— maybe he never did call Aglaea and freak out. He pinched his arm, just to make sure. Nope, definitely not dreaming. Mydei must've gone insane, then.

"You made food for me?" Phainon asked, bewildered Mydei's expression made it look like Phainon was the one out of his mind.

"Yes, is that so hard to believe?"

"Of course it is! You hate me!"

Mydei inhaled sharply and turned around. "Think of this however you want to, then."

Phainon moved toward the table apprehensively, "Is it part of the agreement Aglaea had you sign?"

There was a long pause before Mydei nodded— too late to actually mean it.

Lunch was a silent affair. The food wasn't as good as it was the previous night— or maybe it was and Phainon was just starving last night. His sense of taste wasn't the best. Mydei occasionally glances at him curiously, like he was expecting some sort of reaction from Phainon. Whatever it was that Mydei wanted, Phainon was not going to give it to him.

Phainon got up first, wordlessly picking up the empty cutlery and cleaning them.

"You look exhausted." Mydei commented, leaning against the kitchen island, holding a glass of water.

Phainon almost dropped the fork he was wiping. "Huh?"

He seemed to be scrutinising Phainon, his eyebrows furrowed, like he was trying to figure something out."Like someone's put you through hell and back."

"How very nice of you to comment on my bed head."

"You bed head's even worse than your face, but that's not what I'm talking about. Your smile is even more forced than normal and the bags under your eyes are concerning."

"Astute observation, my dear Mydei." Phainon scoffed.

Mydei rolled his eyes and walked to the couch, muttering what must be Kremnoan curses under his breath.

Phainon should've gone back to his room and done something else, rather than continue this conversation— but something in him wanted to stay. So, he said the first thing that came to his mind to give him an excuse to stick around.

Phainon fidgeted awkwardly with the hem of his sweatshirt, speaking with the sunniest voice he could muster up."Hey— do you go to the gym in this apartment? The facility is kinda far away and I don't want to make that trip other than for lessons and training. Like, I can afford transport to the center, but only for a round trip if you get what I mean. Also, I don't have much on me to afford a gym membership right now—"

Mydei looked up from his phone, placing it back down on the couch.

"Your point being?"

"Stop cutting me off, I was getting to that." Phainon frowned, all pretenses of joy dropping "You're so impatient."

"HKS. If you want me to bring you along as a guest, just say so."

"Uh, can you do that?"

"Yes."

Well, that was easy.

Phainon really didn't want to be alone, so he flopped down on the couch next to Mydei. Mydei didn't react, so Phainon took it as an okay. This temporary truce felt peaceful. Neither spoke or moved from the couch.

Phainon's phone buzzed, and the gag notification sound Hyacine and Castorice had set for him played on full blast. Right there. In front of Mydei.

Phainon clamped a hand over his phone's speaker, but the damage was already done. Mydei looked up, startled by the volume. He could feel Mydei's eyes trailing after his retreating figure.

Phainon slammed the door behind him the moment he entered his room. He slumped to the floor, his back against the door.

Messages from Castorice and Hyacine flooded his phone.

A sharp knock on his door felt like a bucket of ice— cold water. "Deliverer, get ready. I'll sign you up for the gym."

Mydei was not a petty person. He respected worthy opponents and accepted his losses with dignity— not that he ever lost.

Phainon, however, made him the pettiest man in all of Amphoreus.

At first, he didn't think much of the white haired man he saw in the distance the first day he set foot into CHRYSOS. Sure, his hair colour was unique and he had this magnetic charm to him that made everyone around him vy for his attention, but he looked like nothing more than a vapid pretty boy. His presence felt like a wisp of air, easily dissipated and dampened.

Mydei had no plans on interacting with any one when at the facility— he just wanted to graduate and get out of there. When the white haired man approached him, Mydei had no interest in small talk. When Phainon, the man with eyes so blue you'd think they glowed at night spoke in that condescending tone with the most unfriendly 'friendly' smile he had ever seen, all Mydei wanted to do was beat that shit eating grin out of his face. Maybe he was still on edge after the events that predated his arrival, but his self control snapped.

As it turned out, Phainon was a hurricane— a torrent of determination and unchecked rage. Back in Kremnos, there was nary a person who could put up a good fight against him, but here this man was, dodging with an uncanny efficiency. He was light on his feet and one of the best fighters Mydei had ever fought with.

Something about the way his smile never truly reached his eyes or his overcompensating tendencies got on Mydei's nerves.

Mydei avoided Phainon as much as he could and yet, he kept falling back into orbit with him. Which was completely out of character for him, because Mydei was rational and should know better.

Said rationality was balled up, crushed and thrown out of the window when he was around Phainon.

He wrote and responded to the hate mail chain on the daily— like he was a kid, still nursing his wounds over a petty fight. Frankly, Mydei was too consumed by his dislike for Phainon to care that the mails sounded progressively less like fighting.

Sometimes, Mydei went as far as to consider Phainon a friend. That thought was instantly stomped on, but it still lingered every time Phainon bragged about his newest 'win'. Their current tally was Mydei—7, Phainon—6. Pathetic that he kept count, really. Years of fighting in a war made him wary of having someone at his back. As frustrating as it was, Phainon was probably the only person he'd trust at his back.

And if he noticed the red that underlined Phainon's eyes or the blank, calculating expression he took on when fighting, Mydei made no such comment.

At this very moment, Phainon's expression was awestruck as he gaped at the lounge entrance to the apartment's gym like it was surreal to him. The facility's gym was no joke either, but Phainon seemed enamored with this one. Some guests were eyeing them warily, although Mydei wasn't sure if it was directed at him or to Phainon. Mydei felt embarrassed at having to chaperone the human equivalent of a Samoyed.

"You're acting like a child, Deliverer." Mydei hissed, trying to distance himself from Phainon by walking a few paces too fast.

"Sue me. Look, there's a ridiculously fancy ceiling decoration, It looks so futuristic." Phainon replied, staring up at the ceiling, starstruck.

"I believe that's called a light."

"Shut up." Phainon's lips pulled into a scowl. Mydei found himself vaguely wondering what they would feel like. "Let me have some much needed whimsy. Not like you'd know what that feels like."

"Whimsy or public nuisance number one? Because you seem to be toeing that line."

Phainon opened his mouth to respond, but they were already at the front desk. Mydei handed his membership card to the lady at the front desk.

"I'm so sorry, but we only offer visitor's passes to our residents' partners." She said after checking Mydei's membership card.

"What?" Mydei asked, disbelieving.

"Oh, that's no problem for us, is it honeycakes?" Phainon smiled sweetly, leaning towards Mydei and wrapping his arm around Mydei's waist.

Mydei froze.

Phainon's hand was on his waist.

Also, honeycakes? really?

He had no idea why the touch felt so natural or why he was blushing, but that was something he was going to dissect later. Mydei cleared his throat and discreetly pinched Phainon's arm as revenge. Mydei watched Phainon struggle to maintain his infuriating smile, taking satisfaction in the slight wince in his expression and sharp breath he took.

"Yes, darling." Mydei grit out in the least murderous voice possible.

Phainon was so dead when they got out of this situation.

The lady seemed to buy their act, turning the registration screen towards them "My mistake, gentlemen, enjoy the amenities."

"Thank you!" Phainon smiled the smile that made half the recruits in the facility swoon.

The second they were out of earshot of the lady, Mydei shoved Phainon off him and shot him a glare that said you're done.

"Don't look at me like that. Mydei, I swear I did it so that I could get in and that was the only viable solution." Phainon rambled, trying to diffuse the situation.

To be fair, Mydei would have done the same thing. Something in him didn't feel like beating up Phainon today— maybe it was because of how Phainon had just begun to look cheerful again. Perhaps he still felt guilty for purposefully giving Phainon burnt and over seasoned lunch— which the guy didn't even seem to register.

So, he took a deep breath and counted to ten, before saying, "A warning would have been preferable."

"Yeah. Got it. I don't know how else to tell you this, but we might have to pretend to be dating so that they don't revoke my visitor's pass."

Oh to blazes with it. He wanted to punch Phainon into tomorrow.

"Phainon, what the hell." Mydei slowly turned around to face him.

Phainon threw both hands in the air, and replied, indignant,"Well, I warned you now!"

Breathe, Mydei, breathe. Do not let this brainless, infuriating little shit get to you.

"Oh come on, Mydei. Just play along for a while. I don't want to be dating you any more than you do."

That stung.

"We're at the gym anyways, so let's box."

"Huh— wait— don't walk away—" Phainon exclaimed, running after Mydei "— where did that even come from?"

"So you're chickening out?"

"I don't chicken out of things."

"Prove it."

That's how Mydei and Phainon ended up wheezing on the floor of the gym. The room felt stiflingly warm after their boxing match. It must've gone on for way too long, because Mydei hadn't felt this exhausted in a while.

"Wanna go somewhere?" Phainon asked, sitting upright and taking off his gloves.

"Yeah, sure." Mydei grunted, pushing himself up as well.

Mydei pretended to not notice the people staring at Phainon as he wiped the sweat off his face and neck. Either Phainon was completely oblivious to the stares he got or he just didn't care.

Not that Mydei cared, of course.

Phainon looked at him expectantly once they emerged from the gym. His head tilted to the side and his piercing blue eyes met Mydei's.

"What?" Mydei asked as they entered the elevator.

"Are we taking the death bike again?"

Right. Mydei had driven like a madman on purpose back then, just so he could enact a petty form of revenge on Phainon.

"Yes. I don't see why you expected anything different."

Phainon deflated at that. Had Mydei been a weaker man, he would have laughed at Phainon's ridiculous disappointed expression. They walked through the basement to get to Mydei's bike.

"The death bike" Phainon repeated, staring the bike down.

Mydei handed a helmet to Phainon. "It's really not that bad, get over yourself."

"You're the one making me a victim."

Mydei fastened his own helmet and started the bike "Get on" He called out.

Phainon took a deep breath and hopped on, wrapping his arms around Mydei's waist. It took every nerve in Mydei's body to force him to not jolt at the contact. It was just his brain messing with him because of what happened earlier.

Nothing else.

It was ten minutes into the ride when Mydei realised he had no idea where they planned to go. This wasn't like him. He usually knew what to do and where to go— because he was expected to be a reliable figure. He was the son of Kremnos' leader, Gorgo. People used to look up to him and rely on him.

"Deliverer! Where are we even going to go?" Mydei yelled over the thrashing wind.

Phainon shouted back, "What?"

"Where. Are. We. Even. Going?" Mydei must've strained his vocal cords shouting that loud.

Phainon went silent for a minute.

"There!" Phainon exclaimed, one hand leaving Mydei's waist to point at a cafe up ahead.

Mydei pulled over and looked up at the sign. It read 'Chimera Cafe'. Not bad— Mydei quite liked the little critters. Next to him, Phainon shook his head after pulling off his helmet. He ran a hand through his white hair that shimmered under the sunset. Sky blue eyes fixed on Mydei's for a brief second before they fixated on the cafe's door. Mydei clenched his fist, his fingernails digging into his skin as he strode past Phainon and into the cafe.

"So have you been here before?" Mydei asked, watching as Phainon sprinted to the first Chimera that entered his line of sight.

"Yep. Cas brought me here a couple times." Phainon explained, crouching down to pet the Chimera. He hung his head in defeat when the Chimera decided it had enough pets and wriggled away. Phainon stood up. "I'll go order something— you're good with anything, right?"

Mydei gave a weak nod, but his mind had latched onto a single word Phainon said : Cas. That must mean Castorice— the one who makes poisons in the lab. Phainon seemed to be close enough to Castorice to call her Cas and go to cafes with her. Mydei had no reason to feel so irrationally jealous of a girl he only knew by name.

A nudge at his calf snapped Mydei out of his thoughts and he looked down to see a little white and grey Chimera with blue eyes blinked up at him. He kneeled down to pet it, which it seemed to love, purring and flopping on its back so he could scratch its stomach. Those blue eyes had not a single thought behind them, Mydei concluded after the Chimera rolled on the floor and collided with the wall. The Chimera blinked once or twice and then rolled over, only to hit the wall again. Mydei chortled. That Chimera reminded him of a certain blue eyed, white haired person.

He picked the critter up, absentmindedly petting it. He walked to a window seat at the cafe and soon enough, multiple Chimeras began to surround him. Soon enough, he was surrounded by a legion of little critters vying for his attention. He did his best to ignore the feeling of eyes burning into the back of his head— they had probably recognised the infamous Mydeimos.

Phainon had returned from the counter and gaped at the sight and muttered "Cute"

It wasn't clear wether he was referring to Mydei or to the Chimeras. Mydei chose to interpret it as the Chimeras.

"It's like you have your own little army of Chimeras." Phainon added, taking the seat opposite Mydei.

"Chimeras can't form an army, Deliverer."

"But what if we took in a bunch of them and trained them to fight?"

"That would be idiotic. Chimeras are helpers, not fighters."

"Okay, okay— but your Kremnoan legion or whatever it is you're called can raise them and train them in the ways of fighting. Trust me, this is an investment that'll sell big."

Mydei stiffened at the mention of his father's troops. He had erased the name from his memory the best he could— trying to forget the senseless bloodshed they reveled in. His mother had raised him to protect the lives of the innocent, not slaughter for glory.

"It's called the Kremnoan Detachment. I was never part of the Legion." Mydei said tightly.

Phainon seemed to have picked up on Mydei's change in demeanor. He immediately began to backtrack.

"I'm sorry— the news talked about the Kremoan Legion and you doing the whole killing-your- father-and-entrusting-Kremnos-to-the-government thing so I thought it was interconnected. It's also been over a year and my memory isn't the best."

"Say, what did the Okhema news describe me as?"

"Uh.. You sure you want to know?"

"Yes."

"The patricidal heir to Kremnos. A brute who finds glory in bloodshed. That's a few I remember."

The casual way in which Phainon listed off these attributes was impressive.

Despite the fact that Phainon knew Mydei's origins, he didn't seem to see him any differently. Or hate him any differently.

Although, Mydei wasn't sure if whatever was going on counted as hate any more.

"No wonder they treat me like I'm infected with some virus."

Phainon's brows furrowed.

"Is that why there are so many eyes on us right now?"

Mydei huffed out a derisive laugh "Why else?"

"Usually, there are eyes on me wherever I go because of the whole Deliverer thing so I thought they were looking at me. After all, attention is attention, be it negative or positive. It stings just the same."

"Hm" Mydei gave the most thoughtful response of his life while petting the Chimera on his lap, watching Phainon stand up to get their order.

"It's quite fascinating how you're so beloved by the Chimeras, though. You seem to like them too." Phainon remarked, returning to the table carrying a neon plastic tray of food.

Mydei shrugged "I do like Chimeras. They're cute."

"You never struck me as the type who liked cute things, but I stand corrected. In hindsight, it suits you." Phainon took a sip of his coffee— or rather, milk with a drop of coffee somewhere in there.

"Suits me? The hell you mean by that?" Mydei asked, reaching for the tray. On it was a familiar drink— pomegranate flavoured milk.

Phainon remembered. That fact should not have made Mydei feel so light— headed.

"I mean— the whole 'likes pink drinks and cute critters thing' works for you." Phainon explained, moving his hands about animatedly.

Mydei pursed his lips, trying to dampen the warmth that bubbled up in his heart.

"Mister Phainon?" A quiet voice asked. A little girl stood by the table, clutching a piece of paper.

Phainon beamed at the girl "Yep, that would be me!"

"I made this for you." She handed him the piece of paper.

"Aw, thank you, little one. I'll treasure this— wait— should I frame your amazing sketch?"

The girl nodded rapidly "Yes, um, I just wanted to say— thank you for protecting Okhema!"

Phainon's expression softened, a rare tenderness in his eyes "I'm honored to protect you." It sounded like he meant every word.

The girl sprinted back to her mother, clinging onto her mother's handbag. She timidly waved goodbye, which Phainon returned.

"Did you see that? I got the best present in all of Amphoreus— look!" Phainon said to Mydei, shoving the drawing in his face.

"Ah, yes, white paper. Because that's all I can see."

"Oh, let me just—" Phainon moved the paper back, waiting for Mydei's approval.

"Very nice. You had better not lose it."

"They love me" Phainon held the drawing up, admiring it.

"Attention seeker."

"No regrets."

Mydei sighed, but didn't retort.

The eyes that bore into the back of his head mattered even less. Phainon's attention was focused on him and only him and that was all that he cared about, really.

If he drove a bit slower on the trip home, he'd never tell Phainon because he still hated him.

As long as it's you

One year ago

Eurypon had put up a hell of a fight, or at least, his guards did. The coward sat behind locked doors, sending his men to shield him as he laid in wait for his inevitable demise.

Mydei had lost count of how many times he had died and revived in battle, charging in as a one man army, his reinforcements on the way. The Kremnoan Detachment's leader was not one to let up— not even in the face of death. Death had no grip over Mydei— the immortal that he was. He would never know what caused his immortality, and that was something he was fine with.

Mydei was in a haze of adrenaline and pure, unfiltered rage. He shoved the doors of Kremnos Industries open— the thud reverberating through the room. Eurypon sat on the velvet recliner, as if he was expecting Mydei.

"You." Mydei snarled

"Come to kill me, my son?" Eurypon's sickly sweet voice made Mydei want to throw up.

"As if I'd come here for anything else."

"You hate me, don't you? For what I did to your beloved mother." Eurypon taunted, holding up a gun.

Mydei lunged forward and grabbed Eurypon's collar, pulling him off his seat. He kicked the gun Eurypon held away and wrapped a hand around his throat.

"I don't hate you. I want you dead. I want your corpse's eyes to be staring into mine instead of that disgusting beady glare. I want you to feel the pain she did and relive it over and over."

"Ha! Spoken like a true, bloodthirsty tyrant. You shall incur the wrath of the underworld, just like I shall."

"If I go to the underworld for this, then so be it. I'll drag you down with me and make you crack your skull open on the landing."

Eurypon's smirk curled into a venomous smile. Mydei wanted to knock each one of those gold capped teeth out of his mouth.

"How bold. The bloodline of Castrum Kremnos' dictators shall reign supreme after all. Perhaps I should have accepted you and raised you to be even better." Eurypon cackled, like the madman he was.

"You're mistaken. I will abdicate the seat as the next leader. Kremnos shall henceforth be under the protection of Okhema's government."

Eurypon was livid. "Mydeimos, you take that back" Mydei's name felt poisonous from his mouth.He tried to break himself free of Mydei's grip, but Mydei's hold was too firm.It was strange. The man who had seemed so large and powerful felt so weak in that moment. The nightmare had lost its fangs and claws and was now trying desperately to escape. Mydei should have felt euphoric that moment— indestructible and infallible. He swallowed, pulling out his own gun.

"Goodbye. I hope that death is crueler to you than you ever were." was the last thing Mydei said before he shot his father dead.

He didn't know how long he stayed in that office with Eurypon's corpse turning cold.

"I did it, mother." He whispered, "Are you proud of me?"

Mydei felt stupid saying that. She was dead and would never know that her son went and avenged her death. He imagined her telling him that she was proud of him and that he was just as strong as she was. He missed her terribly, unable to erase the memory of her corpse in his arms or the finality of her being gone forever.

"Mydeimos, I know it must be hard to lose your mother, but you have a detachment to lead. Please pull yourself together and tell us what to do."

Krateros stood by the door of what used to be Gorgo's room. Mydei was seated at her desk, reading over every last letter she wrote to document the progress of the Detachment. He had already memorised the contents of the letters— but he read them over and over again as if doing so would bring her back to life.

"Patience, Krateros. Her funeral rites haven't been carried out yet and you still expect me to move on from her death like it never happened?"

"No. You have every right to mourn her, but you have hundreds to lead. They've begun to seek counsel from you."

"So you're telling me to put duty above my mother? Duty above being human?" Mydei hated how his voice cracked at that last bit. He's felt this white hot rage when he found out that she was poisoned by Eurypon. Mydei was prepared to rip Eurypon from limb to limb if he had to. Now, any semblance of fight had dissipated from his system, leaving behind jagged, broken pieces he wasn't sure he could ever put back together.

"I'm telling you to step forward and lead."

"…Give me a day. A day to peacefully mourn Kremnos' greatest warrior."

"A day? People have lost entire bloodlines overnight and have had to stand up and fight when the sun rose. You are a Kremnoan— to fight back is in your nature." Krateros paused, taking a deep breath "Please weigh the well being of your people with your selfish desires. You are young— barely fifteen— but you have a nation to eventually conquer"

With that, Krateros closed the doors behind him and left.

Was it really selfish to want to mourn his mother? Was he being selfish because he wanted to act like a child and cry in someone's arms until he shattered?

Yes.

He would be selfish if he were to dedicate himself to something that wasn't his people.

But why couldn't he just be a normal person, just once?

How would he react, Mydei wondered long after his tears ran dry, if he told Krateros that he truly didn't want to reclaim Castrum Kremnos.

Now, years later, he knew the answer.

Krateros paled, going through a catalogue of emotions ranging from horror to rage before settling to incredulous.

"Would you repeat that?" He asked, voice strangled.

"I'm placing Castrum Kremnos under the protection of Okhema's government." Mydei repeated. He was older and surer of himself, no longer the child nursing the pain of losing his mother all alone. "There is no guarantee that I won't become like Eurypon. Kremnos will be better protected from the Black Tide."

"Please reconsider—"

"—no. Kremnos' legacy of patricide and bloodshed ends here and now. That is my first and last order."

Krateros went silent for a long time, grieving the loss of all that he knew, believed in and lived for. When he spoke, his voice was resigned.

"What of you?"

"I will assist my people in settling in. Once that's done, I'll enroll in CHRYSOS so I can get the qualifications needed to eliminate the Black Tide."

"You.. really have this planned out, don't you?"

"Yes."

For the first time, Mydei couldn't bring himself to care if people thought he was being selfish.

✶⋆.˚⋆⭒˚.⋆ 𖥔🍷 ݁𖥔 ݁✶⋆.˚⋆⭒˚.⋆

Present day

It had been a little more than a week since Mydei realised his feelings for a certain douche bag named Phainon. Said douche wasn't making it any easier on him. Mydei would get flash banged by Phainon's smile at every turn and even in the privacy of his own home. That man burned with the brightness of a million suns.

Sometimes, Mydei wondered how long it would be until the sun died out or got eclipsed.

Phainon seemed to be growing progressively more anxious about something. He would sometimes stare off into space during their daily gym visits and wake up and pace around the house in the odd hours of the night. Mydei had almost jumped out of his skin when he first bumped into Phainon pacing in the hallway in the dark, his eyes wide and haunted. That was an incident neither of them mentioned again. Even then, the bite in his emails never lessened.

Phainon physically dragged Mydei to the test results board the minute they set foot in the CHRYSOS facility.

"HKS, your palm is sweaty. Let go of my hand." Mydei complained, trying not to overthink the contact.

"Sorry, sorry" Phainon mumbled, letting go of his hand.

Mydei found that he missed the feeling of Phainon's hand in his. Phainon scrutinised the board before sighing in defeat, tapping his foot against the floor in an infuriating rhythm. The results still weren't out yet.

"Deliverer, is this was you've been anxious about all week?" Mydei asked, bemused.

"No— I was just anxious to beat you in this test. Yes. That's all." Phainon had the subtlety of a brick to the head.

"Did you think you did bad in this written test?"

"I might have messed up with the formulae."

"…I'm not the greatest at numbers."Mydei had no idea why he was trying to comfort his academic rival, but here he was anyway.

Phainon's eyes widened "You're bad at math." His face lit up and he let out a soft, disbelieving laugh.

Mydei clenched his teeth. That was exactly what he was trying to convey, but upon the wrath of Nikador, Phainon did not have to phrase it so directly.

"Shut up." Mydei restrained himself from reacting harshly. They were in public. The other recruits were going to stare and point at them if he caused a scene.

"Oh. My. Titans. You're bad at math." Phainon repeated, tasting the words on his tongue.

"It's not like I got that many opportunities to learn math while training to be a warrior."

"Makes sense, but even then— hey! Where are you going, Mydei?"

Mydei stopped in his tracks and turned around to respond.

"I have a counseling session with Professor Anaxa." Sure, the session wouldn't start for the next ten minutes, but he needed any excuse he could get.

"Oh, alright then. Shame I won't be able to see the expression on your face when you find out that I've beaten you in the test." Phainon paused, the gears in his head turning. A devilish grin replaced the sweet smile he usually wore "But you'll know when I win."

"I don't want to be privy to the thoughts in your head, so I'll make my exit." Mydei deadpanned.

It was Mydei's fault for finding even that cursed grin hot.

He entered the counseling room before Professor Anaxagoras did. Warm rays of sunlight streamed into the room, making it glow in the morning light.

"Oh. You're quite early." Anaxagoras' voice sounded from behind him.

"Yes."

"Good. Let us begin the session. Since you've kept up with the course relatively well and—"

Professor Anaxagoras' words were cut off with a 'ding' from Mydei's phone

"Sorry" Mydei muttered

"As I was saying—"

He was cut off yet again with another 'ding'

Mydei pursed his lips into a thin line.

Then, all hell broke loose.

Mydei's phone buzzed repeatedly, the notifications flowing like a raging waterfall. He knew exactly whose fault this was. Mydei had given up on the notion of silencing his phone and the damage was already done. Why not go the full hundred miles and let the messages pile up?

"You gonna answer that?"

"Leave it."

"… are you sure?"

"Yes."

Phainon was beyond dead the minute Mydei got out of this situation.

Mydei stormed out of the counseling room as soon as the session ended. He was a man with a mission. Phainon was nowhere to be seen— not by the vending machine or training room or lecture rooms. After sprinting through the facility and covering every possible room, Mydei took a seat at a cafeteria bench and decided to go through the messages.

Phainon ˂phainon.419@email.com˃11:55 AM to me▼

HAHAHAAAA I WINNN I GOT MORE THAN YOU IN THE TEST

Phainon ˂phainon.419@email.com˃11:55 AM to me▼

IMAGINE LOSING COULDN'T BE ME

Phainon ˂phainon.419@email.com˃11:55 AM to me▼

LMAOOO YOU SHOULD SEE THE SCORES I WISH I WAS THERE TO RECORD YOUR REACTIONN

Phainon ˂phainon.419@email.com˃11:56 AM to me▼

Did you see the scores yet?? Did you see?

The rest of the emails were just about the same. Mydei groaned, putting his head in his hands and questioning everything that led him to this point.

Why he still found himself attracted to this dolt was beyond him.

Out of the corner of his eye, he noticed two girls walk into the cafeteria. The purple haired girl seemed to recognise him and nudge the bubblegum haired girl.

The bubblegum haired girl greeted him first "Hi! You must be Mydei. I'm Hyacine— I work in the med bay. This is Castorice." She gestured to the other girl , who bowed her head slightly as greeting. This must be the Castorice Phainon spoke so affectionately about. No, Mydei was not jealous. He was a stronger man than that.

"We've heard so much about you from Phainon" Hyacine chirped as she and Castorice joined Mydei's table. He didn't recall offering them seats there. Mydei's eyes caught onto the fat white horse keychain hanging off Hyacine's bag. He'd seen the same overweight horse everywhere around Okhema— advertising Okhema Pharmaceuticals co.

"Hold on, is that Ica?" Mydei asked, pointing to the keychain.

"Yep! It's my family business' mascot."

So Hyacine was the heiress to a prestigious corporation. Now he was starting to understand why Phainon seemed nonplussed by Mydei being the son of a dictator. No, he still didn't fully understand why Phainon actively sought out the presence of the son of a war criminal. Even then, Phainon must have gotten used to the glamour of the title and learned to see the person underneath it.

"Interesting. If I may ask, why this horse?"

"Oh, little Ica's actually been with us for years, so my parents put them as the mascot. Honestly, having a cute horse helps with the brand image and better yet, I get to see Ica on the big screen."

"I see."

Mydei reverted back to silence. He wasn't, by any means, the most tactful in holding up a conversation.

"So…How have things been with Phainon?" Castorice questioned in a soft voice, determination overtaking her shyness.

"What do you mean?"

"You know, your boyfriend." Hyacine stressed on the last syllable.

Mydei choked on air.

"My— what? I can assure you, there is nothing going on between us. Where did you even get that idea from? "Mydei sputtered

Castorice and Hyacine exchanged a knowing glance.

"Oh, just from the way he talks about you." Hyacine shrugged, trying to play it off.

Mydei wished his heart would stop thudding in his throat, restricting his words."He talks about me?"

"For the past few months, you've been a common topic." Castorice nodded, typing something on her laptop.

"Oh."

"We haven't been able to talk to you thus far because of a certain someone begging us to never interact with you. But he isn't here right now, so it's free real estate." Hyacine said as she pulled out her notebook and pens.

"What exactly does he say about me?"

Castorice looked up from her laptop, briefly pausing her typing,"Well, first it was about how much he hated you. Now.. it's kinda hard to tell because he still complains about you, but it's significantly less hostile."

Mydei raised his eyebrows "He still complains about me? Let me guess, it's because I nagged him for forgetting to do the laundry last week. Or maybe it's because I drive too fast. Well, tell him that I have a bone to pick with him for the stream of messages I just received." He paused, "Tell me, is he always this annoying?"

Castorice shook her head " He acts this way only around you."

"Yep. He never struck me as the petty or childish type. Matter of fact, it took forever for me to even think he considered me a friend and not a friendly acquaintance." Hyacine added, tapping her pen against the desk.

Mydei wondered if Phainon thought of him as a friend. Well, he made Phainon food and went to the gym with him. Even better, they found a system for cohabitation and they worked together quite well. Yeah, that should count as gestures of friendship.

Truth be told, Mydei didn't exactly make appetising meals for Phainon when he did something particularly stupid— which was most days. The dolt somehow didn't notice, savouring Mydei's cooking like it was ambrosia and staring at him, doe eyed from behind the counter as he awaited his meal.

They also got into fights and sent death threats via email.

Never mind, then.

"You two seem to have known him for a while now. How long have you been in the CHRYSOS training facility?" Mydei asked

"I joined here when I was nineteen. Cas has been here since she was seventeen. So it's been about four years since I first met Phainon."

"Say, what was he like back then?" Mydei couldn't help prying a little bit into Phainon's past.

Castorice patted her bangs down and answered, "About the same, honestly. He was so outgoing and popular that I didn't expect him to try to talk to me."

"Phainon's always been in the spotlight— you know, with the whole new 'hope' of Okhema thing. Someday, he'll take over the CHRYSOS facility and lead the efforts against the Black Tide. He's all over social media for that very reason." Hyacine said.

"Is he really?"

"You didn't know?"

"I don't really use social media."

"And he hasn't told you that he has multiple fan pages?"

"He has multiple what now?"

"He was just as surprised as you are when he learned about their existence."

"I had no idea he was this popular. I mean, I knew he was popular, but not to this extent." Mydei mused.

"You're plenty popular, too. I mean, you would've been the leader of a nation and that's no small feat. Most of the recruits are too scared to even approach you because you're so… Cas— help me here—"

"—accomplished." Castorice supplied

Hyacine's face brightened "Yeah. Accomplished."

Mydei didn't think the recruits avoided him because he was 'accomplished'. The people in Okhema hated him for being Kremnoan and for his not so stellar reputation. Therefore, the recruits either hated his guts or were terrified of him, but he decided to humor Hyacine and Castorice anyway.

"That makes sense."

Nobody talked for a while after that. Mydei pretended to be engrossed in reading something on his phone to feel a little less out of place among the scratch of pens and the clack of typing. Castorice giggled at her laptop and tilted it to show Hyacine something. They exchanged triumphant grins.

"We'll have to go now." Castorice announced in her soft voice, standing up. "It was a pleasure talking to you."

"You're quite unlike the rumors. Phainon was right when he said that you could be rather sweet." Hyacine smiled warmly at Mydei.

Phainon said he was sweet?

✶⋆.˚⋆⭒˚.⋆ 𖥔 ݁☀️𖥔 ݁✶⋆.˚⋆⭒˚.⋆ Phainon wasn't a failure after all. The score board felt surreal. His bundled up nerves felt pointless now that he stared at the results.

20)Phainon— 60 points

21)Mydeimos— 58 points

He won.

He won.

"No way… Phainon didn't get first place?"

"Mydei didn't either. That's insane."

"I think the sun rose in the west today for that to happen"

"What could've happened for both of them to score this low?"

Forget the bewildered glances thrown his way. Reputation paled in comparison to winning against Mydei.

That was a statement Phainon never thought he would make.

With a giddy grin on his face, Phainon fired off email after to email to Mydei. If only he could see Mydei's expression right now. Probably murderous.

Good.

Phainon won and he would lord it over Mydei as much as he could and it wasn't because he was incredibly insecure and needed to feel like he was better than the man he declared as his rival.

WHAT YOU GUYS NO YOURE NOT SUPPOSED TO TALK TO MY MORTAL ENEMY. HE'S MY RIVAL— WHOSE SIDE ARE YOU ON?? I DIDNT BEAT HIM IN THE TEST FOR NOTHING

Please no I'm dying over here

No response for hours after that. Phainon may be regretting this.

"HKS!"

Mydei must've returned. And by the way he sounded, he was pissed.

Phainon rose from the sofa, prepared to make a run for it. Mydei's footsteps grew louder until there he was, dropping his bag and glaring daggers at Phainon.

"Where. Were. You." Mydei scowled, the pretty lines of his face creasing.

"Haha.. I was at the facility all day. So whatever do you mean, my dear Mydei?" Phainon drawled. True, he had been at the facility all day— just hiding out of Mydei's sight.

"You are so dead for sending me those messages." Mydei stalked to the couch.

"Oh come on, it was a wonderful joke." Phainon said, circling around the couch with Mydei.

Mydei cracked his knuckles.

Mydei climbed over the sofa and grabbed the front of Phainon's jacket, pulling him towards him. Phainon wriggled out of Mydei's grasp and dodged his next punch. Phainon laughed gleefully as he landed a hit on Mydei. Mydei lunged at Phainon again and he tried to dodge. Phainon's leg caught on the arm of the sofa as he moved back and he toppled backward onto the sofa— dragging Mydei down with him.

Mydei breathed heavily, his blonde hair falling over his face. His lips quirked into a victorious half smile as he pinned Phainon to the couch.

Phainon ascended to a higher plane of existence that very moment.

Shit. Why was Mydei so hot?

Phainon gaped up at Mydei, like all words failed him. His mind must have rebooted serval times, but to no avail. All he could think of was how pretty and gorgeous and hot and ethereal Mydei looked in that moment. Mydei huffed and got up. He ran a hand through his messy blonde hair — which was the single hottest thing he could possibly do. Phainon sat up slowly, his head reeling. His throat felt drier than sandpaper and he had a hard time focusing.

"Admitting defeat already? That's a new record." Mydei's voice broke through the cloud in his brain. Phainon's mind pinpointed on Mydei's voice and only his voice like all he wanted to focus on was Mydei.

What the hell was wrong with him?

Phainon opened and closed his mouth to retort, but no words came out. The gnawing feeling of embarrassment resurfaced and he averted his gaze.

Phainon coughed awkwardly, forcing words out of his mouth "That— that didn't count."

"Sure. I won this time, though. Me—11, You—9." Mydei stated, tilting his head to the side—making his hair braid cascade fully onto his shoulder.

"Unfair."

"What's unfair, Deliverer?"

"You."

"Uh huh. Keep saying that to yourself." Mydei snorted

Phainon's phone rang. It was Aglaea. He still wasn't over the embarrassment of the last call, but he knew better than to ignore the call.

"Hello?"

Aglaea wasted no time in getting straight to business. "Yes, good evening, Phainon. Two weeks from now, there will be a meeting with the Council of Elders. Our purpose is to make an appeal to keep the CHRYSOS facility running since they're trying to shut it down."

"Oh." Phainon thought back to the conversation he had overheard ages ago.

"Since you're the face of this operation, it would be ideal to have you present and make your own statements."

"I'm honored, Aglaea. I'll do it." Not agreeing was not an option. Aglaea wanted him there, so he would do it. End of story. His fear of public speaking be damned— this was his reputation and likeability on the line.

"That's good. You will have to argue against the Council's spokesperson and give an ending speech." She paused, "Also, I haven't heard from you since that call. Are you sure everything's fine?"

Phainon gulped, he did not need to be reminded of that— especially in front of Mydei. "Yes. That was a lapse in my judgment. For that, I apologise."

Aglaea stayed silent on the other end for a while.

"Alright then, thank you, Phainon."

Phainon put down the phone and ran a hand over his face. This was going to be like a big debate, right? He could do debates. He was good at debates. But a debate with high profile people who would probably look down on a simple country boy and could easily wipe him off the map?

Phainon had half a mind to ring up Aglaea and tell her he'd changed his mind.

"You look lost" Mydei commented after watching Phainon in silence.

"How am I supposed to go up there in a big fancy suit and argue with the literal government?"

"Not the government, it's a political party."

"They're equally intimidating, Mydei."

Mydei paused, considering something

"I'll help you figure out what to say."

"Yes, please."

"All right. First, do not show fear. Do everything to act like you belong there and let nobody question you." Mydei said, leaning over the couch as Phainon feverishly typed out everything Mydei said on his phone. He could feel Mydei's hair tickling his neck.

Phainon swallowed.

This was not going to be an easy two weeks.

On this particular day, Mydei was scrutinising the suit Phainon planned to wear for the meeting. Phainon felt weirdly exposed as Mydei observed him.

He stood there, fidgeting with the fraying collar, looking everywhere but directly at Mydei's golden eyes.

Mydei physically dragged him to the mall, Phainon's excuses falling on deaf ears. But then again, Phainon wasn't going to complain about being pulled along by Mydei.
